description: MUST-FAIL: identifier grammar, trailing newline. Section 4.1 declares the bare representation to be a 64-character lowercase hex string and states the listed representations are distinct and not interchangeable; section 6.1 requires a verifier that finds the carried identifier inconsistent with the established context to NOT report the reference as verified. A 65-character string whose last character is U+000A is not a 64-character lowercase hex string: the verifier MUST reject it, not strip the newline and compare the remainder. Only a MUST-FAIL vector can discriminate here -- a tolerant verifier accepts every input a strict verifier accepts.

registry_entry.name: cpb-day2-artifact
registry_entry.digest_context: jcs-n; empty exclusion set; 64-char lowercase hex

note: The first 64 characters are the correct digest; the realistic provenance is an identifier read from a file written by a shell redirect. This vector is also the regression test for the checker's own identifier grammar: with a ^...$ anchored pattern Python's $ matches before a trailing newline, so the checker itself would classify this carried representation as syntactically valid bare hex. The pattern must be anchored with backslash-A and backslash-Z.
